title: River Life Operating System Commerce Integration
purpose: Integrate a governed commerce path that converts verified provider payment evidence into the existing canonical River order and fulfillment domains without allowing payment-provider details to redefine fulfillment correctness.
governingPrinciples: Payment and fulfillment remain separate concerns.
Provider-specific payment payloads must be authenticated or otherwise verified before they can authorize a paid River order.
Provider-specific payment payloads must be normalized before entering the canonical River fulfillment domain.
The canonical RiverOrder contract established by PRODUCT-001D remains authoritative.
Duplicate provider events must not create duplicate canonical orders, entitlements, fulfillment requests, or deliveries.
Provider retries and event redelivery must be safe under stable provider payment identity.
A provider event must not authorize fulfillment unless its normalized payment state is paid.
A paid order must resolve to an explicitly approved product release before fulfillment.
Commerce integration must preserve the private source manuscript boundary.
Secrets, webhook verification material, and private provider credentials must never enter public client bundles or static repository content.
A public price or purchase path must not be activated merely because provider integration code exists.
Commerce readiness must be demonstrated end-to-end before public purchase authorization.

commerceDomain.providerEventIdentityRule: A provider event identity must be stable enough to recognize provider redelivery without creating a second commerce effect.
commerceDomain.providerPaymentIdentityRule: A provider payment reference may resolve to only one canonical River order.
commerceDomain.canonicalOrderIdentityRule: Repeated normalization of the same legitimate provider payment must recover or reproduce the same canonical River order identity rather than create a second order.
commerceDomain.orderIdentityDriftRule: An existing canonical order identity may receive legitimate payment-state updates but may not silently drift across provider identity, customer identity, product identity, price identity, or currency identity.

providerSelection.rule: Existing Stripe-hosted contribution-link architecture is prior evidence for contribution flows only and does not itself select Stripe for PRODUCT-001E product commerce.

runtimeBoundary.currentSiteRuntime: Astro static output deployed through Cloudflare assets
runtimeBoundary.rule: PRODUCT-001E must not pretend that the current static asset runtime can securely receive and verify private payment events without an explicitly selected server-side execution boundary.

implementationSequence.name: Commerce payment-event contract foundation
implementationSequence.outcome: Provider-independent payment-event identity, verification state, normalization inputs, and canonical RiverOrder mapping rules exist in code and deterministic tests.

implementationSequence.name: Payment provider selection and adapter
implementationSequence.outcome: A concrete payment provider is selected deliberately and isolated behind the provider-independent commerce contract.

implementationSequence.name: Verified payment-event ingestion
implementationSequence.outcome: Provider payment events can enter through a server-side verification boundary and unverified events cannot authorize paid orders.

implementationSequence.name: Durable commerce persistence integration
implementationSequence.outcome: Verified provider event identity and canonical order state can be persisted and recovered safely across retries and event redelivery.

implementationSequence.name: Checkout mechanism
implementationSequence.outcome: The selected provider can create or expose the minimum governed checkout path required for the River Life Operating System without activating public commerce prematurely.

implementationSequence.name: Paid-order fulfillment integration
implementationSequence.outcome: A verified paid provider event can normalize into the canonical RiverOrder and enter the existing PRODUCT-001D fulfillment orchestration without redefining fulfillment semantics.

implementationSequence.name: End-to-end commerce readiness gate
implementationSequence.outcome: Commerce may advance toward public product presentation only after checkout, verified payment evidence, canonical order persistence, approved release resolution, entitlement creation, and recorded delivery can be demonstrated safely and idempotently.

product001fHandoff.title: Product Presentation and Public Launch Path

publicationBoundary.reason: PRODUCT-001E establishes commerce integration. Public product commerce remains unauthorized until the end-to-end commerce readiness gate and the later PRODUCT-001F presentation and launch gates explicitly permit publication.

completionCriteria: Provider-specific payment evidence normalizes into the canonical RiverOrder contract.
Provider payment identity cannot create duplicate canonical River orders.
A concrete payment provider and checkout mechanism are selected deliberately.
Provider-specific commerce details remain isolated from fulfillment-domain semantics.
Verified paid orders can enter existing PRODUCT-001D fulfillment orchestration.
Commerce persistence survives retry and event redelivery.
Secrets and customer commerce data remain outside public static content.
Price, availability, checkout publication, and customer purchase remain unauthorized until explicitly advanced through the publication boundary.
